content: 1. Darunavir increases the levels of mirtazapine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased toxicity. Liver function tests (LFTs) should be monitored, and caution is advised during coadministration. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may elevate the risk of adverse reactions. Close monitoring is recommended. 3. Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine via CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, when coadministered with mirvetuximab soravtansine, may increase exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of the antibody-drug conjugate. This can heighten the risk of adverse effects. Monitoring is essential. 5. Mitotane decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be required, and monitoring is advised. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of inhaled mometasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction raises the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects, including Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 7. Darunavir also increases the levels or effects of inhaled mometasone via CYP3A4 inhibition. The potential for increased toxicity warrants careful monitoring. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of intranasal mometasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 9. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal mometasone through CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Nafcillin decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required during coadministration. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitoring for adverse effects is necessary when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. 12. Darunavir increases naldemedine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein modulation. Monitoring for adverse effects is recommended. 13. Darunavir decreases the effects of nateglinide, potentially due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Hyperglycemia has been reported. Monitoring is advised. 14. Nefazodone increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases nefazodone levels via the same mechanism. Monitoring is required. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs may increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitoring is necessary. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitoring is advised. 18. Darunavir and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Darunavir also increases nevirapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitoring is required. 19. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 21. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Dosage adjustments of nilotinib may be necessary. 22. Darunavir increases the levels of nintedanib by modulating P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Adverse effects may require dose reduction, therapy interruption, or discontinuation. 23. Nirmatrelvir increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients on ritonaviror cobicistat-containing HIV regimens should continue their treatment as indicated. Monitoring for adverse events is necessary. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic norgestrel concentrations, raising the risk of adverse effects. Monitoring is recommended. 25. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nortriptyline. Careful dose titration of the antidepressant is necessary, starting with the lowest feasible dose and monitoring its response during coadministration. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Less frequent dosing of oliceridine may be necessary. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 28. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Adjust oliceridine dosing as needed. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 30. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease ondansetron clearance, but no dosage adjustment is recommended. Monitoring is advised. 31. Orlistat decreases darunavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. 34. Oxcarbazepine decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Oxycodone dose reduction may be warranted. 36. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 37. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 38. Darunavir increases the levels of panobinostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required due to the potential for increased toxicity. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of paroxetine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect. Monitoring is necessary. 41. Pentobarbital decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is required. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of perphenazine. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be needed. 43. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pitavastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Start with the lowest recommended dose of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and titrate while monitoring for safety. 45. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of pitolisant by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, and monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), a CYP3A4 substrate. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, raising the risk of toxicities. Monitoring is necessary.
